reviewed_by: Claude Code, fixing the ~18 minute post-deploy 'Project execution is reconnecting' outage on live Apple Bug Bounty
reason: After the 42d2bb4 deploy, Apple Bug Bounty's recovered worker answered 503 'reconnecting' for ~18 minutes. Root cause (independently validated by a fresh subagent from raw Postgres lock-wait logs): once a recovery is verified and activation starts, the worker reports 'prepared' until its lifespan finishes, and the supervisor's handoff loop re-selects it every 0.5 s. Each pass ran _recovery_grant(check_blockers=True), which holds the project's ownership row FOR UPDATE (fenced) through _recovery_blockers' project-wide scan of chat_turns/chat_goals payload->>'execution_claim_id' (4-7 s on 3.4M rows, json payloads). Every worker transaction takes FOR KEY SHARE on that row, so activation ran one transaction per ~5.7 s supervisor cycle (193 holder transactions x 5.7 s = 18.3 min, matching the window). Fix: when the recovery is verified and the worker reports activation_started, skip the blocker check and the repeat verify/activate; a later pass marks it activated once ready. A verified recovery that has not started activating still checks blockers (an uncertain effect still holds activation). Selected: a new focused test of _advance_project_recovery plus the supervisor recovery suites (controls, recovery, reconciliation).
exclusions: test_runtime_continuity_acceptance.py needs a production UI build and complete source, so it is not selected. 3 PostgreSQL cases in test_recovery_controls.py (pause_and_stop_run_while_recovery_is_blocked, held_worker_activates_only_after_blockers_resolve, held_target_that_ran_a_control_and_then_failed_exits) fail identically on pristine origin/main; PostgreSQL cases skip in CI without NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL. All SQLite cases pass locally with the fix. No UI change.
